task.title: Bind claimed-schedule consumption to exact revisions
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/811 by preventing an earlier claimant from releasing or materializing a later claim after an ABA lifecycle cycle.
acceptance_criteria: Expose the current persisted schedule revision as read-only caller evidence.
Require the exact observed claimed revision for release and materialization.
Reject stale claimants with typed concurrent-modification evidence and no release, schedule, or orphan task write.
Keep revisions separate from worker identity, permission, leases, clocks, recovery policy, dispatch, and execution.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused test build failed because ScheduledTask::revision and revision-bound release and materialization APIs did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added ABA release and materialization tests, including an assertion that rejected stale materialization creates no orphan task.

attempts.diagnostic: A schedule ID identified the aggregate but not the exact claim observation authorized for consumption.
attempts.patch: Exposed persisted revisions, centralized revision validation, and guarded release and materialization with the caller's exact observed revision.

attempts.diagnostic: The substantive CodeRabbit walkthrough reviewed all five changed files and generated no actionable comments.
attempts.patch: Retained the bounded revision-authority contract after independent review found no blocking correctness, concurrency, authority, test, or documentation issue.

outcome.summary: Claim-consuming schedule transitions now fail closed when a caller presents stale claim evidence, including after release and reclaim cycles.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test -p vela-kernel --test schedule_store stale_claim_revision

lessons: An aggregate identity is not sufficient concurrency authority when one lifecycle can return to the same claimed state.
Validate the observed revision before lifecycle-state interpretation so stale evidence reports a concurrency conflict rather than consuming newer state.
Atomic materialization must reject stale schedule evidence before creating the paired task stream.
A persisted revision proves which observation is being changed; it does not identify a worker or grant execution permission.
